name: AXE AI | Email Intake → Drive + Sheets Orchestrator Final

parameters.content:
## Reuse-or-create + watermark + single-path consolidation

**Reuse-or-create:** before, every run unconditionally created a new client root folder, attachments subfolder, and conversation sheet -- even for a client that already had them, duplicating everything and re-logging their entire history the moment `Processed` got reset to false. Now, each of the 3 resources is preceded by a Find -> Pick Exact Match -> If Found trio (same pattern already used in drive_shopify_image_sync.json's 'Find Category Folder'/'Pick Exact Category Match'). Found -> reuse its id, skip creating. Not found -> create exactly as before. Downstream nodes read from a stable '... (Resolved)' node instead of the Create node directly, since the Create node no longer always runs. New accounts with no existing folder are unaffected -- same create + full-history-fetch behavior as before.

**Watermark:** the control sheet needs a `last_synced_at` column (manually add the header -- blank = new account). Gmail search is scoped to `after:<date>` when present; each successful run writes the new `last_synced_at` back alongside `Processed: true`.

**Outlook watermark:** Microsoft Graph won't combine $search (needed for "from OR to" matching) with $filter (needed for a date range) in one request, and toRecipients isn't $filter-able at all -- confirmed against Graph's docs. So Outlook still calls the API with the full-history search, but 'Normalize Outlook Messages' filters the results client-side against last_synced_at before anything gets queued.

**Single-path consolidation:** this workflow used to have two nearly-identical parallel paths -- a "single-provider" path (triggered when Platform was exactly "gmail" or "outlook") and a "merged" path (triggered otherwise, handling accounts active on both providers). The only reason two paths existed was that the merged path's account-splitting logic did `JSON.parse(Platform)`, which throws on a plain "gmail"/"outlook" string -- not an actual difference in what needed to happen. That parsing was made tolerant of both a plain string and a JSON array (treating a plain string as a single-element array), so the merged path's already-optional-chained gmail/outlook handling now correctly covers the single-provider case too. The single-provider path (its own copy of the reuse-or-create trio, its own Gmail/Outlook search+normalize, its own queue/mark-processed nodes -- 39 nodes) was deleted; every account now goes through what used to be only the "merged" path. 82 nodes -> 43, no loss of behavior.

**Not yet addressed:** per-message/per-attachment dedup for anything that still gets queued despite the watermark (Outlook's full-history refetch, or anything the Gmail date-scoping doesn't catch) -- relies on the Gmail/Outlook Processor Final sub-workflows, not yet implemented. Also, nothing resets `Processed` back to false automatically -- still a manual action; the watermark only matters once someone does that for an account that already has infrastructure.

**Drive scoping audit (no global search):** confirmed every Google Drive operation in this workflow is parent-scoped, none search Drive-wide. Search nodes (`📂 Find Client Root Folder`, `📂 Find Attachments Subfolder`, `📂 Find Conversation Sheet`) all set `filter.folderId`. Create nodes (`Create Client Root Folder`, `Create Attachments Subfolder`) and `Move Sheet to Client Folder` all set an explicit parent `folderId`. The only exception is `Create Conversation Sheet` (Google Sheets node) landing wherever the credential's default location is on creation -- the Sheets API has no create-with-parent option -- but `Move Sheet to Client Folder` relocates it into the resolved client root folder immediately after, in the same execution.
Folder hierarchy (top -> bottom): `1a6nPIjW5VLARperP9yrSqXJMDmfojqUl` (top-level Axe AI parent -- corrected; superseded 1y59d2aX1VjhHGX3L0hDUhpeO0PqbzxWr, which was the older/wrong top folder) contains the 3 provider parents used as `folder_id` in 'Combine Gmail & Outlook Per Client' -- gmail-only `1-1EdTSWeoFPnbRa_hKdYsX4aMnqiQSSE`, outlook-only `1L5xu6tTaS6yZXbHpTrpE4IQ1xjV8G_J8`, combined `102oeld1yMYGMmWs2Od198HqO1KeVhv_n` -- each of which contains that provider's per-client folders, each of which contains that client's attachments subfolder + conversation sheet. Every search/create already resolves within this tree, so no change was needed to scope things "inside this folder" -- it already was.

**Fixed: zero-new-messages stalled the loop.** Root cause identical in shape to the earlier "empty Platform kills the loop" bug, just one stage later: `Expand Gmail Message IDs` / `Expand Outlook Message IDs` return 0 items when an account has no new mail on that side, and by default n8n doesn't run a node at all when its only input produced 0 items -- so when BOTH sides are empty (nothing new anywhere for that account this cycle), `Merge Expanded Messages` never fires, which means `Queue Messages` never fires, which means `Mark Account Processed` never fires -- and since `Mark Account Processed` was the only thing looping back into `For Each Account`, that account (and every account still left in the batch) stalled silently, exactly like Michael Latifi's case did earlier. Fixed by turning on "Always Output Data" on `Merge Expanded Messages` (so it emits one placeholder item instead of nothing when both sides are truly empty) and adding `❓ Any New Messages?` right after it, gating on `{{ $json.id }}` notEmpty: real messages -> unchanged path through `Queue Messages` -> `Mark Account Processed`; no messages -> straight to `Mark Account Processed`, bypassing `Queue Messages` entirely so the placeholder item never risks writing a blank row into the queue sheet (the same mistake "Always Output Data" caused once already, when it was tried on `Queue Messages` directly instead).
